audit.whatIsWrong: Four places call Granite Shield his W (whys[3], wants.foe[0], and 'blocked-by-W-shield' / 'his W armor' in early and mid). Granite Shield is Malphite's passive; his W is Thunderclap, an attack-speed aftershock effect. The page also never states what the shield is worth or how it comes back.
audit.why: The shield is the reason Neeko's poke feels like it does nothing, and it recharges only if he has not been hit for a few seconds — that is the whole poke rhythm of this lane, and it is unusable advice while the ability is filed under the wrong key.
audit.corrected: whys[3], wants.foe[0], content.early, content.mid and breakdown.cooldowns now name Granite Shield as the passive, worth 10% of his max health, and state the recharge condition.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats Unstoppable Force as an unanswerable button ('his R is unstoppable and interrupts your Pop Blossom channel', 'never ult ON him while his ult is up') and never mentions the range collision that decides level 6.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force carries the dash flag and travels 1000. Tangle-Barbs roots at exactly 1000 and a root stops a dash. That makes the level-6 exchange a race between a 12s ability and a 130s one — the single most valuable fact available in this matchup, and the mirror already states it from Malphite's side.
audit.corrected: whys[4], spikes[1].text, wants.you[2], content.mid and breakdown.cooldowns now state the root-cancels-the-dash race with both ranges and both cooldowns.
sources: kit: Malphite R dash flag, range 1000, cd 130/115/100

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid and wants.you[2] tell the player to bait Unstoppable Force with the clone — 'use W (Shapesplitter) clone and invis to make him blow his unstoppable engage on a fake'.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force is launched at a location, not at a unit, so a clone cannot draw it. Following this advice means holding Shapesplitter for a bait that cannot happen instead of holding the root that genuinely answers the dash. The mirror's author found the same thing from the other side.
audit.corrected: wants.you[2] now holds Tangle-Barbs for the dash, and content.mid states that the ult is location-targeted.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart sides Neeko at level 6 and Malphite at 2+ items, while the packet chart and the mirror both read Malphite at 6 and Skill at 2+ — and whys[4] on this very page says his R flips the all-in, while whys[6] says it 'nets to even on positioning'.
audit.why: Both rows contradict their own why text. Level 6 belongs to whoever casts first, and a 130s ultimate that knocks up beats a Neeko who opens with Pop Blossom; at two items the fight is decided by spacing, which is what Skill means.
audit.corrected: win[4]/phases[4].side to Malphite and win[6]/phases[6].side to Skill as matched pairs, ratings rescaled.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.diff reads HARD while diffRating says 4/10 and both rating lines say 'Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10'.
audit.why: The verdict field and the numbers beside it disagree, and the chart backs the verdict: Malphite owns four of seven stages against a 48.48% win rate. Nothing here is favoured.
audit.corrected: diffRating 4/10 to 6/10, carryRating 5/10 to 6/10, both rating lines to 'Hard matchup'.

audit.why: The packet's suspectNames flag on 'Seismic Shard' is a false positive — that is Riot's real name for his Q.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are your only proving ground here. Malphite stacks armor, not magic resist, so your Q (Blooming Burst) re-blooms hurt his low base MR every time he steps into melee CS — chunk him at level 1 while he has no escape and you only fear his single-target threat. The trap is his Q (Seismic Shard) slow: once it lands he sticks to you, so throw your E (Tangle-Barbs) from max range or not at all, because a blocked-by-W-shield, walked-out root is a wasted skillshot. Don't dive his minions; just poke and make his armor stacking feel pointless.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are your only proving ground here. The trap is his Q (Seismic Shard) slow: once it lands he sticks to you, so throw your E (Tangle-Barbs) from max range or not at all. Poke on a rhythm too — Granite Shield is 10% of his max HP and recharges whenever he goes a few seconds unhit.

edits.before: This is where he claws even and ahead. At 6 your landed E into Pop Blossom is genuine burst, but his R is unstoppable and will interrupt your channel mid-windup — never ult ON him while his ult is up, or he flips the all-in and bursts your squishy body. Bait the R first: use W (Shapesplitter) clone and invis to make him blow his unstoppable engage on a fake, THEN root and combo. His Q slow plus W armor make him sticky and tanky enough that your single rotation often won't kill, so play poke and roams, not a forced 1v1.
edits.after: This is where he claws even and ahead. At 6 your landed E into Pop Blossom is genuine burst, and the order decides it: Unstoppable Force is a dash, so a landed Tangle-Barbs cancels it outright — your 12s against his 130s, both reaching 1000. Root first or don't commit. Don't try to bait the ult with a clone either; it is aimed at a location, not at you, so the decoy draws nothing. His Q slow and armour keep him sticky enough that one rotation often won't kill, so play poke and roams, not a forced 1v1.

edits.before: - Malphite Unstoppable Force: matchup-defining — Unstoppable engage — usually banked for teamfights, punish lane passivity. Check it before every step-up. - W clone + disguise is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Malphite Unstoppable Force: matchup-defining — 130s at rank 1 over 1000 range, and it is a dash, so your 12s Tangle-Barbs reaches exactly as far and cancels it. - Granite Shield is 10% of his max HP and recharges when he goes unhit — never let him idle.

notes: The best thing on this page now is the range collision: Tangle-Barbs and Unstoppable Force both reach 1000, and a root stops a dash, so level 6 is decided by cast order rather than by who is stronger. The two flagged interactions I could not fit anywhere length-safe: Thunderclap (W) applies on-hit and is an attack reset, so his burst tell is the early attack; and Ground Slam scales its damage off his armour, which is why building armour items makes him hit harder rather than just tankier. Whether Unstoppable Force's knock-up can interrupt Pop Blossom's preparation is not stated in either kit — I removed the claim rather than assert it.
